verdict.rationale: dlt is built for bulk/batch data movement — pipelines load lists of records, tables from SQL databases, files from cloud storage, and REST API pages in bulk, with incremental loading, merge/upsert, and schema evolution handling large datasets automatically (dlt-docs-1, dlt-docs-7, dlt-docs-18, dlt-docs-27, dlt-docs-39). This is fundamentally a bulk-ETL tool, so batch operations across many records/tables are core. However, the story frames 'bulk operations across many items' from an AI-native/agent-driving perspective, and evidence for agent-driven bulk orchestration (e.g., agent triggering many pipelines/backfills at once, or bulk operations via MCP tools) is limited to single-pipeline deploy/monitor commands and one read-only SQL query tool, not explicit multi-item batch agent actions. missing for 10: explicit evidence of agent/MCP tools performing bulk operations across many pipelines/tables/backfills simultaneously, and independent/hands-on confirmation of bulk-scale reliability beyond docs.
